claims.statement: All Seoul upstream calls are made by five exported fetch functions in apps/api/src/upstream (fetchStopCatalog, fetchNearbyStops, fetchArrivals, fetchSubwayArrivals, fetchSubwayStationCatalog), each of which takes the fetch function as its first argument, returns normalized types from @mota/contracts, and is called by TransitController or TransitCatalogService with options.upstreamFetch injected through API_OPTIONS (defaulting to global fetch in AppModule.register).

Each upstream endpoint has a fixed purpose, method, timeout, and response cap: fetchStopCatalog GETs selectNearStops.do with kiloMeter=45 and lati=37.55/longi=127 under a 30 s timeout and 10 MiB cap; fetchNearbyStops GETs the same URL with kiloMeter=radius/1000 under 8 s with no cap; fetchArrivals POSTs form-encoded arsId to getStationByUid.bms under 8 s with no cap; fetchSubwayArrivals GETs /v1/seoul-subway/arrival under 8 s with no cap; fetchSubwayStationCatalog GETs the T-Data download.do?id=10229 CSV under 15 s with a 1 MiB cap.

Every adapter call sends the shared UPSTREAM_HEADERS constant { Accept: "application/json", "User-Agent": "mota/0.1 (+https://mota.m16khb.xyz)" } (with fetchArrivals additionally adding a form-urlencoded Content-Type by spreading it), and passes signal: AbortSignal.timeout(...) as the only latency bound — there is no retry, circuit breaker, or other timeout mechanism in this layer.

Adapters classify failures by throwing UpstreamError(message, detail) for non-2xx statuses and over-cap bodies, and TransitController converts every adapter failure (UpstreamError, Zod throw, timeout, network error) into HTTP 502 with body { error: "UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE", message: <Korean string>, detail: errorDetail(error) } via BadGatewayException.

The same selectNearStops.do endpoint serves both bus modes, differing only in query parameters, timeout, cap, and normalization: fetchStopCatalog uses BUS_CATALOG_LOCATION (lat 37.55, lng 127, radius 45_000) to request the full 45 km catalog, while fetchNearbyStops scopes the identical URL to the user's location with kiloMeter = radius/1000 (e.g. radius=800 becomes kiloMeter=0.8).

TransitCatalogService.nearbyStops falls back to the location-scoped live lookup fetchNearbyStops only when the bus ManagedCatalog read throws an UpstreamError (cold load failure, count-gate rejection, or byte-cap trip); non-UpstreamError failures are rethrown and surface as 502. transit-catalog-fallback.e2e.test.ts pins this by asserting the same mocked fetch was called first with kiloMeter=45 (the rejected catalog attempt) then kiloMeter=0.8 (the live fallback for radius=800), and that the response was 200.

The subway catalog path has no live fallback: GET /api/subway/nearby propagates subway.read() errors to TransitController, which converts them to 502 UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE, because the T-Data CSV is the only station source.

The two bus normalizers parse differently by design: normalizeNearbyStops strictly parses the whole ResponseVO.data.resultList envelope so one bad row fails the live response, whereas normalizeStopCatalog parses a looser z.array(z.unknown()) envelope and then per-row safeParses with nearbyStopSchema, keeping only complete rows so one bad row cannot discard the citywide catalog.

normalizeOfficialSubwayStationCatalog strips a leading UTF-8 BOM, then strictly validates the first CSV row as a five-column Zod tuple of the literals 외구간_역_수, 역한글명칭, 호선명칭, 환승역X좌표, 환승역Y좌표; any renamed, reordered, or truncated column set throws and fails the whole catalog load.

After the header check, each station CSV row is safeParsed as a tuple of [code, name, line, lng, lat] and malformed rows are silently dropped while valid rows are kept; the resulting id is prefixed seoul-<code> and the X/Y coordinate columns map to lng/lat respectively.

officialLineName strips a trailing parenthetical from the CSV line name and then applies two renames on ingest: 분당선 becomes 수인분당선 and 수도권 광역급행철도 becomes GTX-A, keeping the catalog's line names consistent with the SUBWAY_LINE_NAMES arrival mapping (1075 → 수인분당선) and with display logic.

The station CSV adapter feeds the subway ManagedCatalog, whose minimumItems gate rejects a wholesale truncation before it can become the cached catalog; production main.ts sets minimumSubwayCatalogItems to 100 (bus to 10_000), while the AppModule.register test default is 1, and the nominal refresh interval is 24 h via TRANSIT_CATALOG_REFRESH_MS.

The subway arrivals upstream is an external proxy (default https://k-skill-proxy.nomadamas.org) whose origin is overridable only via SUBWAY_ARRIVAL_UPSTREAM: the adapter always appends the fixed path /v1/seoul-subway/arrival via new URL, so any path in the override value is discarded. The override flows loadEnv (z.string().url()) → main.ts → AppModule.register → ApiOptions.subwayArrivalUpstream → TransitController, which passes it as the adapter's third argument; compose.yaml does not set it, so production uses the default origin.

apiStationName() rewrites exactly three saved station names to their parenthesized official API names before the upstream URL is built — 천호 → 천호(풍납토성), 군자 → 군자(능동), 총신대입구 → 총신대입구(이수) — passing every other name through unchanged; the e2e test asserts the resulting percent-encoded URL byte-for-byte.

fetchSubwayArrivals discards the updatedAt computed by normalizeSubwayArrivals (derived from the max upstream recptnDt) and returns new Date().toISOString() instead, because upstream data timestamps can lag receipt by minutes and both the client's 90-second freshness rule and the elapsed countdown key on updatedAt — a lagging data timestamp would mark fresh data stale and drop imminent trains. TransitController.busArrivals performs the equivalent receipt-time stamping for the bus route.

GET /api/arrivals/:arsId and GET /api/subway/arrivals hit their live upstream on every request and are never catalog-cached, whereas GET /api/stops/nearby and GET /api/subway/nearby are answered from the in-memory catalogs and only touch an upstream during warmup, stale, or scheduled refresh.

The two catalog byte caps are enforced after the body has been fully read into a string, by re-encoding with TextEncoder and comparing the byte length to BUS_CATALOG_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES (10 MiB) or SUBWAY_CATALOG_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES (1 MiB); they reject a misrouted or oversized payload from becoming the cached catalog but do not stream-limit the download.

The adapters contain no Zod of their own: every upstream schema and normalizer lives in packages/contracts (src/bus.ts and src/subway.ts), which import only Zod and their own modules, per the AGENTS.md boundary rule.

The subway arrivals row schema is strict about the stable identity keys subwayId, updnLine, trainLineNm, and recptnDt (each must be present and non-empty) while defaulting or nullable-ing volatile fields (btrainSttus, barvlDt, arvlMsg2, arvlMsg3, lstcarAt); a row missing an identity key therefore throws, which the controller maps to 502 UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE rather than returning partially-keyed rows.

Bus arrival rows are parsed tolerantly: rawArrivalSchema is .passthrough() with defaults for sparse fields (adirection → 방향 정보 없음, arrmsg1 → 운행 정보 없음, arrmsg2 → "", busType1/congetion1 → "0", plus arrmsgSec1/2, sectOrd1/2, routeType), so a sparse Hermes BIS row normalizes instead of failing the response.

Only one upstream leg is plain HTTP — the Hermes BIS arrivals endpoint http://m.bus.go.kr/mBus/bus/getStationByUid.bms — while the other four endpoints use HTTPS; and no adapter sends credentials or an API key, so there is no secret management for this integration.

The adapter AbortSignal deadlines are the operative latency bound because the Fastify requestTimeout of 65 s configured in main.ts sits above all of them (8 s live, 30 s bus catalog, 15 s subway catalog), so an adapter deadline fires before the server-level timeout.
